how_it_works: The Experience section is built around TWO vertical rails running down the viewport with a shared, top-to-bottom TIME axis (this pattern is the rare case where the block reads CHRONOLOGICALLY earliest→present rather than reverse-chron, because the whole point is that two separate origins converge into one present — the merge must land at the bottom/'now'). LEFT rail = the clinical thread (maroon #8B2E2A): Andhra Medical College bedside/hospital reality. RIGHT rail = the technical thread (ink #0E1116): DEXTER ML → nference technical work. Each rail is a 1px stroke drawn as an SVG <path fill:none>; each career beat is a card anchored to its rail by a small date node. The signature move is a merging WEAVE: near the bottom (the nference full-time 'Junior Clinical Data Scientist' beat) the two rails bend toward the center seam, braid over/under each other (exactly the existing WeaveDivider motif: over-strand + a masked gap in the under-strand at each crossing so it reads as passing BEHIND, not a flat X), and resolve into ONE unified stroke — the visual argument that clinical + technical fused into clinical data science ('systems that reach the bedside'). CRITICAL overlap handling: because AMC Clinical Intern (Apr 2025 – Mar 2026) and nference Intern (Oct 2025 – Apr 2026) run concurrently, the shared time axis places BOTH beats at their true vertical positions so they visibly coexist side-by-side across the same Oct 2025–Mar 2026 band — a faint horizontal date gridline (mono year/month label in the gutter) ties the two rails at that latitude so a recruiter instantly sees 'she was doing both at once' rather than a false sequence. Motion is content-driven, NOT a full-section pin: the page scrolls naturally; two cheap scrubbed layers ride along — (1) each rail draws top-to-bottom via stroke-dashoffset/drawSVG bound to ScrollTrigger scrub as you read, and (2) the weave/merge strand at the bottom draws-in ONCE when it enters. Cards reveal once on entry (opacity/y). Earliest beats (Animations Media healthcare ops Jan–Feb 2025, DEXTER Feb–Mar 2025) sit at the top before the rails have fully separated. On mobile the two rails collapse to a single spine with a left/right or tagged marker (◀ clinical / technical ▶) per beat and the overlap shown as two stacked-but-date-stamped cards — no horizontal braid on small screens.
visual_structure: A single beat = [date node on its rail] + [content card offset to the outer side of that rail]. Card contents, top→bottom: date range in JetBrains Mono meta (e.g. 'Apr 2025 — Mar 2026', muted #5A5A5A), role title in Fraunces (the anchor), org in Inter, 1–3 tight Inter bullets, optional mono proof chip (DEXTER '~90% test acc'). Rail assignment encodes the thesis: LEFT/maroon = clinical (AMC bedside; carries the signature ECG hairline accent, one use only); RIGHT/ink = technical (DEXTER TensorFlow CXR CNN; nference LLM extraction / multi-AMC SQL cohorts). nference intern sits on the technical rail as a 'promoted from intern' continuity sub-beat directly under the nference FT beat (same org, two date ranges — not two disconnected cards). The OVERLAP band (Oct 2025–Mar 2026) is the visual centrepiece before the merge: AMC card on the left and nference-intern card on the right sit at the same vertical latitude, joined by a faint dotted horizontal date tie so the concurrency is unmistakable. The MERGE point is the nference FT 'Junior Clinical Data Scientist' beat at the bottom: the two rails braid over/under at the center seam and become one maroon+ink stroke leading into it, and this beat can be a slightly larger editorial 'present' card centered on the unified line. Whitespace is generous (editorial-minimal); the two thin rails + one weave carry the structure, not boxes or logos.
motion_recipe: GSAP + ScrollTrigger + DrawSVGPlugin only (no framer-motion) — reuse the exact primitive already in the repo: src/components/signature/weave-divider.tsx braids a maroon CLINICAL path and an ink TECHNICAL path with a mask punching gaps at crossings and animates drawSVG '0%'→'100%'. Rails draw: gsap.fromTo(rail, {drawSVG:'0%'}, {drawSVG:'100%', ease:'none', scrollTrigger:{trigger:'.rails', start:'top 80%', end:'bottom 40%', scrub:1, invalidateOnRefresh:true}}) — one per rail so both trace as you read (doubles as reading progress). Weave/merge strand: draw ONCE on entry, gsap.fromTo(strands,{drawSVG:'0%'},{drawSVG:'100%', duration:1.1, ease:'power2.inOut', stagger:0.08, scrollTrigger:{trigger:mergeEl, start:'top 85%', once:true}}) — mirrors WeaveDivider. Card reveals: per-card ONCE, gsap.from(card,{opacity:0,y:24,duration:0.6,ease:'power2.out',scrollTrigger:{trigger:card,start:'top 75%',toggleActions:'play none none none'}}), stagger via ScrollTrigger.batch (~0.1); nodes pop scale 0.6→1 ease:'back.out(1.5)'. The overlap date-tie fades in once with the second of the two overlapping cards. AMC ECG accent: stroke-dashoffset draw-in once (~0.9s power1.inOut) on the AMC node — NO infinite pulse loop. Section titles use existing BlurText. DO NOT: pin the whole section and scrub-scrub the whole timeline (scroll-jack, kills recruiter skim), animate width/height/layout (transform+opacity only for 60fps), infinitely loop the ECG or the weave, or use MorphSVG to morph the two rails into one (a drawn braid-then-merge reads clearer and is far cheaper than point-matched morphing). Optional Lenis synced via gsap.ticker + lenis.on('scroll',ScrollTrigger.update), gated behind reduced-motion.
reduced_motion: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, render the fully-resolved end state statically (wrap all gsap/ScrollTrigger/DrawSVG setup in gsap.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)') and in the reduce branch just gsap.set(rails+strands,{drawSVG:'100%'}) — the same escape hatch WeaveDivider already uses). Both rails, the braided weave, and the merged unified stroke are painted at rest; all cards at opacity:1/y:0; the AMC ECG shown as a static drawn glyph or omitted; the overlap date-tie shown as a static dotted line. Skip Lenis, use native scroll. Nothing that carries meaning is hidden behind motion: the two labelled rails, the side-by-side overlap band with its date tie, and the visible merge into one line still communicate the entire clinical+technical→converged thesis with zero animation. On mobile/reduced-motion the collapsed single-spine variant (per-beat ◀clinical/technical▶ tag + explicit date ranges on the two overlapping beats) preserves both the chronology and the concurrency.
brand_fit: HIGH — this is the single most on-thesis Experience pattern for Madhavi's clinical-AI portfolio, and it is uniquely 'hers' rather than a recognizable template. Reasons: (1) It literally IS the brand thesis (duality as structure → convergence): the diptych spec calls 'clinical ↔ technical duality as structure' the best brand-thesis fit, and this pattern makes the whole Experience block state that argument. (2) It reuses an existing signature primitive — the WeaveDivider already braids maroon 'clinical' + ink 'technical' into one merged stroke — so the motion vocabulary is consistent, dependency-free (GSAP already in stack), and proven. (3) It's editorial-minimal and reduced-motion-safe by construction (once-reveals + scrubbed hairlines, no pin/scroll-jack, no purple SaaS glow). (4) The AMC ECG accent has a natural home on the clinical rail (signature, one use, not spam). Risks to manage, which is what keeps it from being trivially HIGH: (a) it inverts the site's reverse-chron convention (needs earliest→present so the merge lands on 'now') — must be clearly labelled with dates so recruiters aren't confused; (b) a two-rail + braid diagram is more novel/complex than a plain spine, so it must stay legible and NOT tip into an infographic gimmick; (c) the overlap band is the highest-value AND highest-risk moment — if the concurrency of AMC + nference-intern isn't dead obvious, the whole 'two threads at once' story collapses into a confusing tangle.
steal: Steal the merging weave itself, powered by the code already in the repo: take src/components/signature/weave-divider.tsx (maroon clinical strand + ink technical strand that braid over/under a masked center seam and drawSVG into one line) and scale it from a divider into the structural backbone of the Experience section, so the two vertical rails visibly converge into a single unified stroke at the nference full-time beat. It's the one detail that turns a generic two-column timeline into a literal picture of the brand thesis ('clinical + technical → systems that reach the bedside'), and it costs almost nothing because the primitive, the palette, and the drawSVG+mask technique are already built and reduced-motion-guarded.
avoid: Avoid letting the AMC + nference-intern overlap read as a sequence or get lost in the braid — if the two concurrent 2025–26 beats aren't pinned to the same vertical date latitude with an explicit tie and visible date ranges, recruiters will misread the timeline (the task's hard requirement is that the overlap stays clear). Equally, avoid over-engineering the convergence into an animated infographic: don't MorphSVG the rails into each other, don't pin the whole section and scrub the entire timeline to the scrollbar (scroll-jack that blocks skimming and re-triggers on back-scroll), and don't loop the weave or the ECG — draw them once and let them rest. The braid is seasoning that makes ONE point (two threads became one); if it competes with the dates and role titles for attention, it becomes clinical-credibility-killing slop.
live_examples: andysenclave/lunar-divide-folio (github.com/andysenclave/lunar-divide-folio) — a portfolio explicitly built on a 'dual-perspective / dual-narrative career story' with two personas (engineering left) tracked along a shared scroll-driven journey timeline; closest published match to the two-parallel-threads-over-one-time-axis idea (though it uses a D3 globe + a 2800vh sticky pin rather than a light-paper braided hairline, and is heavier than Brand_Kit allows). [uncertain] shadcn.io 'Timeline Branching' and 'Dual Track Comparison' blocks (shadcn.io/blocks/timeline-branching, /blocks/timeline-comparison) demonstrate the split-into-parallel-lanes-then-reconverge and side-by-side dual-track-with-connectors layouts respectively — good structural references for the fork/merge and the horizontal date-tie, but they're generic component demos, not clinical-AI portfolios, and lean on Framer Motion. [uncertain] For the merging-strands craft itself, the 'DNA synthesis' / double-helix scroll pieces (e.g. the Astro+GSAP+Lenis 'Brutalist/Industrial' developer portfolio described at ide.com, and shadcn.io/background/dna) show two sinusoidal strands assembled reversibly on scroll — apt biotech metaphor and technique reference, but far more maximalist than the restrained maroon/ink weave this pattern calls for.
